items.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024
items.q: And all of a sudden Freddie Green walks in.

ctx.x: Yes. And on occasion we get to be in front of our musical heroes, which I did once with Cannonball Adderley, who is still my guy. Addendum, separate insert follows:

Count Basie was coming to Kansas City and because we had played all those Sammy Nestico charts in the high school band, I knew who — Count Basie, I’d read about Count Basie and the connection to Kansas City that I thought for the school newspaper I was going to write a big history of Kansas City jazz and this would be great if I could interview Count Basie then that could be a part of my Kansas City jazz history and it’d be really great in high school to be able to do that. So our principal knew somebody and was…

which I heard him do many other times but I didn’t know this at the time but I heard him do this in many other interviews, “Oh well you see I’m writing a book. I’m writing my biography, and I can’t talk about those things that are going to be in the book, so you got any more questions? And of course you can imagine like a 16-, 17-year-old kid that has — and I don’t know what to do. So I kind of re-phrased the question. I guess I don’t know what I said but I kind of re-phrased it. And then Basie goes, “You know…
